insights.title: The first model was tested on genomes it had seen
insights.text: The original forecaster reported AUC 0.93 from a random row split. On genomes it trained on it scores 0.94; on genomes it never saw, 0.64. Every result on this site now uses a genome-grouped split, so no genome is on both sides.

insights.title: The complete data is a harder, fairer test
insights.text: On the complete data (cleaning v7: 5.0x the rows, 439,542 genomes, resistant share 36% to 28%), 22 of 24 runs score lower (median change -0.037 AUC) and the order of methods is unchanged; only Ablation: antibiotic only and A12 unseen genus did not drop. The v5 numbers were optimistic, not wrong.

insights.title: Lab-confirmed results are predicted far better
insights.text: On v7 the best model scores 0.785 on all test rows but 0.919 on the rows with a real laboratory result. Most test rows carry labels BV-BRC predicted by computer, which these features predict less well. Quote the lab AUC for claims about real isolates.

insights.title: The algorithm matters less than the data
insights.text: On the same 400k-row sample, LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost and random forest land within 0.003 AUC of each other (0.777 to 0.780); logistic regression trails at 0.765. Tree ensembles win, but which one barely matters.

insights.title: More rows stopped helping early
insights.text: AUC goes from 0.776 with 50k training rows to 0.781 with 200k and 0.782 with 800k. Better features, not more of the same rows, is the way up.

insights.title: The MIC and the organism carry the signal
insights.text: Knowing only the antibiotic and its class gives 0.657. Every feature except the MIC (organism, resistance rates) gives 0.775, and adding the MIC lifts it to 0.785. The organism does most of the work; the measured MIC adds the rest.

insights.title: A genus it never saw is still hard
insights.text: With every Klebsiella genome held out of training, AUC on Klebsiella is 0.618. The forecaster generalises to new genomes of organisms it knows, not to new organisms.

insights.title: The genome beats a gene lookup table
insights.text: On the same lab-tested genomes, calling a strain resistant whenever it carries a gene of the drug's class scores 0.711; organism and drug alone reach 0.834; the learned genes model scores 0.979. A lookup rule over-calls resistance; learning which genes matter for which drug is what works.
